# Viral hemorrhagic fevers

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Infectious diseases > Zoonoses and vector-borne diseases > Viral hemorrhagic fevers*

[Original Article Link](/library/aL0Qwg)

---

## Summary

Viral hemorrhagic <u>fevers</u> (VHFs) are a group of viral infections caused by <u>viruses</u> from five different families: <u>Arenaviridae</u>, <u>Bunyaviridae</u>, <u>Filoviridae</u>, <u>Flaviviridae</u>, and <u>Paramyxoviridae</u>. The most well-known VHFs are <u>Lassa fever</u>, <u>Hantavirus</u> syndromes, <u>Ebola virus disease</u>, <u>Dengue hemorrhagic fever</u>, and <u>yellow fever</u>. Transmission of VHFs occurs via contact with their animal or insect reservoirs or <u>vectors</u> (e.g., rodents, mosquitoes, ticks). Human-to-human transmission is also possible, e.g., via bodily fluids. VHFs predominantly occur in tropical and subtropical regions. <u>Clinical features of VHFs</u> vary but often include an initial nonspecific <u>flu-like</u> illness that progresses to multisystem hemorrhage. VHFs are diagnosed via <u>antibody</u> detection (e.g., <u>IgG</u>, <u>IgM</u>), <u>PCR</u>, or <u>immunohistochemistry</u>. Treatment is typically supportive, but antivirals may be used in some cases (e.g., <u>ribavirin</u> in <u>Lassa fever</u>). <u>Case fatality rates</u> vary greatly between VHFs but can be up to 90%. <u>Vaccines</u> are licensed internationally for <u>yellow fever</u> only, so prevention primarily consists of <u>infection control</u> measures.

## Clinical features

<u>Clinical features of VHFs</u> vary depending on which <u>virus</u> is involved. Onset may be acute (e.g., <u>Ebola virus disease</u>) or insidious (e.g., <u>Lassa fever</u>) and often includes the following:




* Initial <u>flu-like</u> illness 

* <u>Headache</u>, <u>dizziness</u>

* <u>Conjunctivitis</u>

* High <u>fever</u>

* <u>Lymphadenopathy</u>

* <u>Sore throat</u>

* <u>Myalgia</u>, <u>arthralgia</u>

* <u>Rash</u>

* <u>Weakness</u>, fatigue, <u>prostration</u>  [[15]](/library/fBXkZ00)

* Gastrointestinal symptoms (abdominal <u>pain</u>, <u>diarrhea</u>; , <u>nausea</u>, <u>vomiting</u>) [[15]](/library/fBXkZ00)[[16]](/library/TBX6Z00)

* Severe VHF with <u>bleeding diathesis</u>: develops in a variable number of cases, depending on the causative <u>pathogen</u>

* Diffuse hemorrhage including:

* Bloody <u>diarrhea</u>, <u>hematuria</u>, <u>hematemesis</u>, <u>melena</u>

* <u>Mucosal</u> bleeding

* <u>Petechiae</u>, <u>ecchymoses</u>

* <u>Hypovolemic</u> <u>shock</u> and <u>multiorgan failure</u>

* <u>Sepsis</u>

* <u>DIC</u>

* <u>Meningoencephalitis</u>

## Diagnosis

* Approach

* <u>Diagnosis of VHF</u> during the early stages is difficult because the symptoms are nonspecific.

* If clinical and laboratory features are consistent with the condition, further studies should be conducted to confirm the diagnosis.

* <u>Medical history</u>

* A detailed travel history to <u>endemic</u> regions is essential!

* History of exposure to a potential source of infection (e.g., rodents, mosquitoes, ticks)

* General <u>laboratory studies</u>

* <u>CBC</u>

* <u>Electrolytes</u>, <u>BUN</u>/<u>creatinine</u>, <u>liver function</u> tests

* <u>Urinalysis</u>

* <u>Coagulation studies</u>

* <u>Confirmatory tests</u>

* Generally performed by specialized reference laboratories; presumptive positive results must be confirmed by the <u>CDC</u>.  [[15]](/library/fBXkZ00)

* <u>Serology</u>: <u>IgM</u> and/or rising levels of <u>IgG antibodies</u> detected using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (<u>ELISA</u>) or other diagnostic assays [[17]](/library/3BXS000)[[18]](/library/RBXl000)

* Reverse <u>transcription</u>-polymerase chain reaction (<u>RT-PCR</u>) [[19]](/library/iBXJ000)

* <u>Immunohistochemistry</u> [[19]](/library/iBXJ000)

---

## Treatment

* Supportive treatment

* Management of fluids and <u>electrolyte</u> balance

* Maintenance of blood pressure and oxygenation

* <u>Analgesics</u> for <u>pain</u> and <u>fever</u>

* <u>Blood products</u> in patients with severe <u>thrombocytopenia</u>, <u>coagulopathy</u>, hemorrhage

* Medical treatment 

* Treat patients with <u>ebola</u> with atoltivimab/maftivimab/odesivimab OR ansuvimab. [[20]](/library/BMVzIE0)

* <u>Ribavirin</u> may be used in <u>Lassa fever</u> and Crimean-Congo <u>fever</u>.  [[21]](/library/QBXu000)[[22]](/library/zRVrp80)





> [!WARNING]
> <u>Aspirin</u> and <u>NSAIDs</u> should be avoided in VHFs because they are associated with an increased risk of bleeding!

---

## Prevention

### <u>Immunization</u>



* See “<u>Vaccine</u>” in “Overview of viral hemorrhagic <u>fevers</u>” above.




### Prevention [[15]](/library/fBXkZ00)[[23]](/library/jBX_000)[[24]](/library/PBXWa00)




* Avoid contact with blood, body fluids, or tissue from infected reservoirs or humans

* Avoid travel to <u>endemic</u> areas

* In suspected cases

* Immediate notification of local health authorities and the <u>CDC</u> of any suspected cases of VHF

* Strict isolation of infected patients and their contacts with <u>disinfection</u> and sterilization measures

* Wear appropriate <u>personal protective equipment</u> (e.g., impermeable gown, gloves, respiratory protection, rubber boots).





### <u>Reportable disease</u> [[25]](/library/4BX3a00)



* Probable, suspected, or confirmed cases of VHFs are notifiable conditions to local and state health authorities, as well as the <u>CDC</u> National Notifiable Disease Surveillance System.
